parameters.query:
-- One claim per episode. claim_ooo_followup is the concurrency guard: it returns NULL when the row
-- was already taken, and a NULL composite makes every join below fail, so the item simply produces no
-- output row. That is the filter -- no Filter node, no SKIP LOCKED, no race.
-- MATERIALIZED so the volatile call cannot be evaluated more than once.
with c as materialized (select public.claim_ooo_followup($1::uuid) as f)
select (c.f).id::text           as followup_id,
       (c.f).attempt_count      as attempt_count,
       sc.external_contact_id   as bison_lead_id,
       camp.external_id         as bison_campaign_id,
       cs.external_workspace_id as workspace_id,
       cs.api_key               as api_key
  from c
  join public.sequencer_contacts sc on sc.id = (c.f).sequencer_contact_id
  join public.client_sequencers  cs on cs.id = sc.client_sequencer_id
  join public.campaigns        camp on camp.id = (c.f).target_campaign_id

-- An OOO reply means "I am back on <date>". A follow-up sent long after that date is not a late
-- follow-up, it is a cold email with a false premise. Expire through the RPC, never with raw DML.
-- 'stale' was added by 20260815c; recover_skipped_ooo_followups deliberately does NOT resurrect it.
select count(*)::int as expired
  from (
    select public.skip_ooo_followup(f.id, 'stale')
      from public.ooo_followups f
     where f.status = 'pending'
       and f.scheduled_for < current_date - ($1::int * interval '1 day')
  ) s

-- Same per-episode rule on the failure limb, carrying the HTTP error into last_error so the reason is
-- readable in SQL rather than only in the n8n execution list. 'failed' is re-claimable by design.
select count(*)::int as marked
  from (select public.mark_ooo_failed(t.id, $2) from unnest($1::uuid[]) as t(id)) s

-- The attach endpoint is per-campaign, the state machine is per-episode: mark each id in the group.
-- mark_ooo_submitted requires status='processing' and raises otherwise, so a replay cannot double-mark.
-- Acceptance is NOT proof of campaign membership (the RPC's own comment) -- confirmation is separate.
select count(*)::int as marked
  from (select public.mark_ooo_submitted(t.id) from unnest($1::uuid[]) as t(id)) s

-- Episodes that are due AND still recent enough to be worth sending. NO LIMIT: the run takes the
-- whole due set. A cap of 100/run was tried first and removed on 2026-08-15 once the arrival rate
-- was measured at 115-130 episodes on a working day - a cap below the inflow does not pace the
-- worker, it guarantees the backlog grows.
-- Catch-up by construction: "<= current_date", never "= today", so a missed run is not a lost cohort
-- (branch L's own sticky note records that bug). The lower bound is the staleness cut: anything older
-- was expired by [S] Expire stale in the same run, so this predicate and that one must stay in step.
-- Inner-joining campaigns drops episodes whose routing has not resolved; they stay 'pending' and are
-- picked up once a routing rule exists (recover_skipped_ooo_followups covers the parked ones).
select f.id::text               as followup_id,
       sc.external_contact_id   as bison_lead_id,
       camp.external_id         as bison_campaign_id,
       cs.external_workspace_id as workspace_id,
       f.routing_key            as routing_key
  from public.ooo_followups f
  join public.sequencer_contacts sc on sc.id = f.sequencer_contact_id
  join public.client_sequencers  cs on cs.id = sc.client_sequencer_id and cs.enabled
  join public.campaigns        camp on camp.id = f.target_campaign_id
 where f.status = 'pending'
   and f.scheduled_for <= current_date
   and f.scheduled_for >= current_date - ($1::int * interval '1 day')
   -- Client isolation, enforced here as well as in the routing data. Found on the first controlled
   -- run (2026-08-15): all three of FortumEnergia's routing rows pointed at GIC's identically named
   -- "OOO automation | *" campaigns, so 95 episodes would have enrolled one client's contacts into
   -- another client's campaign. Only Bison's 403 stopped it, and only because the api_key belongs to
   -- the contact's workspace. client_ooo_routing has no constraint tying campaign to client, so this
   -- predicate is the worker refusing to be the vector while that is fixed.
   and camp.client_id = cs.client_id
   and sc.external_contact_id is not null
   and cs.api_key is not null
 order by f.scheduled_for, f.id

with due as (
  select f.id                        as followup_id,
         sc.external_contact_id      as bison_lead_id,
         c.external_id               as bison_campaign_id,
         f.routing_key               as routing_key,
         cs.external_workspace_id    as workspace_id,
         f.target_campaign_id is null as unrouted
  from public.ooo_followups f
  join public.sequencer_contacts sc on sc.id = f.sequencer_contact_id
  join public.client_sequencers  cs on cs.id = sc.client_sequencer_id and cs.enabled
  left join public.campaigns      c on c.id = f.target_campaign_id
  where f.status = 'pending'
    and f.scheduled_for <= current_date
),
payload as (
  select coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
           'workspace_id', workspace_id,
           'bison_campaign_id', bison_campaign_id,
           'bison_lead_id', bison_lead_id,
           'routing_key', routing_key,
           'followup_id', followup_id
         ) order by workspace_id, bison_campaign_id, bison_lead_id), '[]'::jsonb) as items,
         count(*)                                  as due_count,
         count(*) filter (where unrouted)          as unrouted_count
  from due
)
insert into public.integration_sync_runs
  (provider, sync_type, n8n_execution_id, status, started_at, finished_at, metadata)
select 'bison', 'ooo_enrol_shadow', $1, 'success', now(), now(),
       jsonb_build_object('phase', 'A1', 'branch', 'S',
                          'due_count', due_count, 'unrouted_count', unrouted_count,
                          'intended_attach', items)
from payload
returning id::text as run_id,
          (metadata->>'due_count')      as due_count,
          (metadata->>'unrouted_count') as unrouted_count

parameters.content:
## Branch S — SHADOW (phase A1) — SENDS NOTHING

Selects the episodes Supabase thinks are due and records the attach requests it WOULD
have sent, into integration_sync_runs (provider=bison, sync_type=ooo_enrol_shadow).

It deliberately does NOT call claim_ooo_followup: claiming moves pending -> processing,
and with no submit the episodes would be stranded. A1 is read-only by design.

WHY A SHADOW AT ALL: two branches resolving DIFFERENT campaigns would enrol one contact
into two sequences and email them twice. Same campaign is a safe no-op (Bison ignores a
lead already in the campaign, ADR-0015 §4). So agreement must be MEASURED before the
POST is switched on in A2.

Compare per run:
  branch S intent -> integration_sync_runs.metadata->'intended_attach'
  branch L actual -> the attach-leads calls in this execution

Expect branch S to have MORE rows: Postgres catches up on missed runs, the sheet does not.
That is branch S being correct. Do not "fix" it.

Repo: docs/reference/n8n/ooo-phase-a.md

## Branch L — Google Sheets (authoritative, phase A)

Reads rows due today from OOO Leads, resolves the campaign from ARM, and POSTs
attach-leads to Bison. THIS is the branch that actually enrols people.

Known defect, deliberately NOT copied into branch S: the due filter is an exact
equality on today-2d, so a missed run drops that day's cohort forever.
